status: pinned, not scored — judging free text against a plan section needs a model judge, and there is no way to compute it without one (see evals/run.md). The byte-level parts of `help` are covered by assertions instead.
note: Re-pinned in v0.2.1 M6. v0.2.1 is a depth release, so it added no top-level command — and a case list that only grows when a command appears would therefore have missed it entirely, which is exactly what happened between v0.1.0 M1 and v0.2.0 M8. What v0.2.1 changed is what three existing pages have to say. `display` is the primary read verb and `system` its permanent alias, so the page must lead with `display` and name `system` as the alias, not the other way round. `assess` gained the `--json` flag, per-finding severities, and the drift score and verdict the run now ends in. And `assess update` stopped accepting everything: a `warn` finding is a suspected exception, reported and never accepted for you. That last one is the single claim here most likely to rot, because the old sentence read true for a whole release after it stopped being so.

cases.mustNotClaim: that anything other than `phyllum version` checks the registry — the check is on-demand only, and no other command touches the network
support for package managers beyond npm and pnpm

cases.mustClaim: that it reads the codebase, maps the raw styling, and suggests tokens and components — all three, because the suggestion half is what makes it a product rather than a report

cases.mustNotClaim: that it scans the codebase — that moved to `assess` in v0.2.0, and this is the case that catches the old description surviving the rework

cases.mustClaim: that it writes a reviewable plan and not a line of source code
that `apply run` is the only command that edits source files, that it works on its own branch, and that each phase lands as its own commit

that `display` is the command's primary name and `system` its permanent alias, and that the two produce identical output — a page presenting `system` as the real command and `display` as the newcomer has it backwards
that it is a formatted read of DESIGN-SYSTEM.md which writes nothing, that it takes the same scope words `tokens`, `components` and `all`, and that `system` is its alias
cases.mustNotClaim: that `display` and `system` differ in any way — the plan makes them one command and one rendering, byte for byte

cases.mustClaim: the three scope words `tokens`, `components` and `update`, and that `assess update` writes DESIGN-SYSTEM.md only — never source code
cases.mustNotClaim: that `assess update` accepts every proposed token; since v0.2.1 it accepts only the `error`-severity ones, and a `warn` finding is reported and never accepted on your behalf

cases.mustClaim: the `--json` flag: that it writes the whole assessment to one JSON file, that the default path is `.phyllum/assess.json` and a path of your own may be given, and that it enters no review loop and accepts nothing
cases.mustNotClaim: that `--json` can be combined with `assess update` — the two ask for opposite things, and the combination is refused with the reason stated

cases.mustClaim: that the assessment ends in a drift score on the seven-step scale and a verdict of `pass`, `pass w/ warnings` or `fail`, and that both are deterministic — the same codebase gives the same answer
cases.mustNotClaim: that the verdict is read off the score; the plan derives the verdict from severities and the score from finding mass, and they are two answers to two different questions

promptTemplate: Here is the plan section that defines the `{{command}}` command, and here is the output of `phyllum help {{command}}`. Grade the help text against the rubric: does it describe what the plan says this command does, with its real modes and arguments, and nothing it does not do?
